note: Penalties a game, per official, HAND-SEEDED. The free football-data.co.uk match records this repository builds referee rates from carry yellows, reds and fouls but NOT penalties, so data/build_refs.py has always written pen:null and carried the previous value forward. A regex in previous_details once stopped matching, every carried value was dropped, and the column has been empty on all three desks since. There is no free feed that would refill it, so these are read off published referee-stat graphics and entered by hand. THE PAID ONE CANNOT REFILL IT EITHER, and that has now been tested rather than assumed: data/probe_penalties.py ran against API-Football on 2026-09-05 and found its only penalty labels are 'Goal / Penalty' and 'Var / Penalty confirmed'. Both are goal-shaped or review-shaped — nothing marks a penalty that was saved or missed — so a count off them is penalties SCORED, while a referee is judged on what he AWARDS. Building the column from that feed would undercount every official by his saved and missed penalties, invisibly. Until a label for penalties that did not score turns up, hand-seeding is the only honest route.
caveats: A THIRD-PARTY GRAPHIC IS NOT A PRIMARY SOURCE. Every figure here was read off a Betting Village Stats fixture card, which states its own scope ('all data taken from 2025/26 Premier League only') but shows no working. Where the same cards quote figures this repository computes independently, they agree closely: across the seven cards carrying full numbers, reds match exactly every time, yellows to within 0.14 and fouls to within 0.21. Four of the seven — Craig Pawson, Jarred Gillett, Darren England and Robert Jones — matched all three of ours to the second decimal. That is corroboration, not verification: it says the two are counting the same season, not that either is right. The second Michael Oliver card (2026-09-05) TIES both outer bounds rather than widening them — it is the card those figures describe — and its own entry records why the tidy explanation for the gap does not survive checking.

SEVEN OF SEVENTY-TWO. The three divisions carry 72 officials between them and this file names seven. The column stays null for the rest, which is the honest state: pen:null means nobody knows, and a zero would mean he has never given one.

NOTHING IS PRICED OFF IT. The pen column is displayed in the three referee tables and read by no model, so a wrong figure here misinforms a reader and moves no probability. That is the only reason hand-seeded third-party data is admissible at all.

entries.caution: THE TWO OLIVER CARDS DO NOT AGREE ON EVERYTHING, AND THAT IS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE THE PEN IS TRUSTED TOO FAR. Against this repository's own counted figures the second card reads fouls 22.93 (ours 22.72, +0.21) and yellows 3.03 (ours 3.17, -0.14), while reds match exactly at 0.07. Those are the widest divergences any card has shown — they sit exactly on the bounds this file already records — so the pen is corroborated by a source that is measurably not counting quite the same matches we are. The obvious explanation was tested and FAILS: if the card simply held one match more than our 29, his yellow total would have to FALL by one to produce 3.03, which cannot happen. So it is a different sample rather than a lag, and the cause is unknown.

entries.caution: PENS AND REDS BOTH READ 0.13 ON THIS CARD. Over his 23 matches that is exactly what three penalties and three dismissals would each produce (3/23 = 0.130), and our independently computed red rate IS 0.13 — so the pair is self-consistent and plausible. It is still a repeated value in adjacent cells, which is also what a duplication slip looks like, and nothing here can tell the two apart. Recorded because the pen column is displayed and never priced; if it is ever read by a model, verify this one first.
